title: Asphalt paver operator roles and responsibilities
intro: The paver operator maintains alignment and a steady process while coordinating the truck and screed crews. Good operation includes noticing a developing problem early and communicating it clearly.

sections.title: Describe how to position Paver
sections.text: Position the paver to the approved starting line and joint with sufficient working room. Check the first pass carefully because it may guide later passes. Avoid unnecessary manoeuvres and abrupt corrections. Confirm the ground support and the whole machine’s clearance, including extensions and attachments.

sections.title: Describe how to ready the Paver
sections.text: Complete prechecks, appropriate warm-up and screed preparation. Heating prevents material sticking to cold plates; overheating can damage the screed. Follow the fitted heating system’s procedure and verify ready status. Set starting supports and thickness through the agreed screed setup; never use an assumed generic block size.

sections.title: Describe how to follow the line
sections.text: Follow the authorized reference, which may be stringline, a suitable edge, laser or other grade/alignment system. Look ahead and make smooth steering changes. Check that the reference remains valid and protected. Automatic controls can follow an incorrect or disturbed reference faithfully, so independent checks remain necessary.

sections.title: Describe the transition process
sections.text: Coordinate truck changes before the hopper starves or receives a sudden surge. The delivery rate, available buffer, paver speed and planned stopping method must work together. Communicate delays early. Follow the machine’s hopper-wing and feed procedure rather than repeatedly cycling wings as a universal habit.

sections.title: Describe how to maintain consistent “head”
sections.text: A consistent head of material in front of the screed supports stable operation. It is the controlled quantity/distribution at the screed, not simply a completely full hopper. Monitor feed sensors, conveyors and augers as fitted. Changes in head, speed and mixture conditions can alter the mat. Coordinate corrective action with the screed operator.

sections.title: Describe positioning of haul trucks
sections.text: Guide haul trucks into the approved alignment using the designated signalling arrangement. Keep people clear of the truck/paver interface and verify clearance before unloading. Avoid impacts that disturb the paver. Raised bodies change overhead clearance and stability considerations; the driver follows the vehicle procedure and site plan.

sections.title: Describe signals/communication
sections.text: Use agreed, deliberate signals that the intended driver can see through the appropriate mirror or communication system. Obtain acknowledgement. A horn’s meaning must be agreed, not guessed. One designated person directs the movement; anyone can call an emergency stop. Lost or conflicting signals mean stop.

sections.title: Identify obstacles and overhead hazards
sections.text: Scan the route and overhead envelope for utilities, structures, branches, attachments, other machines and people. Account for the truck body, hopper wings and screed extensions as they move. Electrical approach limits depend on the actual system and required controls; do not substitute a guessed distance. Escalate an unresolved obstacle before entering its zone.

worked.title: Hopper level is not the whole story
worked.case: The hopper contains mix, but the right side of the screed has a visibly reduced material head and texture changes.
worked.solution: Report the side and location, coordinate with the screed operator and inspect the feed-system status from safe positions. A full hopper does not prove uniform delivery across the screed. Use authorized adjustments and record the response; do not reach into the feed system.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between hopper contents and head of material.
activities.answer: The hopper receives/stores incoming mix; conveyors and augers deliver/distribute it to the screed. Head refers to the material in front of the screed. One does not guarantee the other is consistent.
activities.title: Explain the difference between hopper contents and head of material.

activities.prompt: A 20 t load lasts 8 min at a steady fictional rate. Find t/min; why is it not a universal paver speed?
activities.answer: 20/8 = 2.5 t/min. Travel speed also depends on width, thickness, density, supply and the approved process; mass rate alone is insufficient.
activities.title: A 20 t load lasts 8 min at a steady fictional rate

activities.prompt: Draft a truck-change handover that includes an access constraint.
activities.answer: Identify machine/lane, designated guide, approach/stop point, protected access, overhead concern, communication channel and lost-signal response. Confirm read-back before movement.
activities.title: Draft a truck-change handover that includes an access constraint.

practical: Align and follow a verified reference.
Coordinate truck transitions and consistent material head.
Recognize and respond to obstacles and communication loss.
